dxgive.evidence_source: [/page/8/Text/10] Planned contrasts indicated that CB group resulted in lower depressive symptom severity than brochure control at posttest (B = −.10, p = .03, d = .29) but not 6-month follow-up (B = −.04, p = .35, d = .12); depressive symptom differences between CB group and CB bibliotherapy were nonsignificant at posttest (B = −.09, p = .06, d = .27) and 6-month follow-up (B = −.01, p = .87, d = .05). Controlling for receipt of adjunctive treatment or intervention credibility, expected benefit, satisfaction with assignment did not eliminate the significant planned comparison of CB group vs. brochure control at posttest. Exploratory omnibus F-tests indicated no overall main effect of Condition on depression symptom severity (F(2, 10821) = 1.28, p = .17) and no Condition X Time interaction (F(2, 13226) = 1.28, p = .28).
